chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Bashar al-Qazvini (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Al-Muzaffar ibn Ahmad and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Suleiman said: They narrated to us Ali ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik al-Kufi, from Al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ali ibn Salim, from his father, that Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Sadiq (peace be upon them) said:

The least thing with which a man might be removed from faith is to sit with a Ghalī (Boaster/Exaggerator), listen to his narration, and affirm what he says. My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), that the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Two groups from my nation have no share in Islam: The Ghalāt (Boasters) and the Qadarites.'

key_terms.أدنى ما يخرج به: The least thing with which one is removed
key_terms.الغلاة: Ghalāt (Boasters/Exaggerators), a group known for exaggerating the status of the Imams
key_terms.القدرية: Qadarites, a theological group denying divine decree (Qadr)

ai.seo_question: Who are the two groups that have no share in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the severity of *ghuluw* (exaggeration) by establishing that merely listening to and affirming the Ghalāt constitutes the minimum threshold for losing one's share of Islam, a concept rooted in the Prophet's warning about two groups excluded from the faith. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on doctrinal purity and the danger of uncritical acceptance of exaggerated claims regarding the Imams' divine status.
